author: calvin
title: Commentary on a Harmony of the Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, and Luke: Luke
edition: Calvin Translation Society, tr. William Pringle, Edinburgh, 1845-46 (3 vols.); CCEL edition
translation: Translated from the original Latin, and collated with the author's French version, by the Rev. William Pringle for the Calvin Translation Society (1845-46)

rights.worldwide: to confirm: death dates of every author, translator and editor named (life + 70 years), William Pringle's among them

notes: Calvin expounds Matthew, Mark and Luke together, section by section (CCEL calcom31 ix, calcom32 ii and calcom33 ii); the 184 sections whose heading names Luke are used. Each of Calvin's lemmas (the bold verse mark, 'Luke 1:5.' or '20.', or the italic words he comments on) opens an entry, with the paragraphs after it, in entries of up to about 350 words; a paragraph cut between entries is marked with ' ...'. A bold mark naming Luke, or a bare verse number while Calvin is on Luke, places the entry on that verse; a mark naming Matthew or Mark turns to that Gospel, and what follows it until the next Luke mark is left to that book. In a section headed first by Luke, the paragraphs before its first mark are on the section's verses of Luke; where Calvin expounds a shared passage under Matthew's verses (as the temptation, Luke 4:1-13), his comment is in calvin-matthew and not repeated here. A page with no heading is placed by its table caption ('Luke 1:1-4'). The Gospel text printed in columns above each section, and the translator's footnotes, are left out. Each entry's heading is the italic lemma as printed.
